answer: Each agent identity must post a refundable bond before it can submit work or claim rewards. The protocol locks the bond in a vault and releases it only after the identity completes a cooling-off period with no duplicate claims; evidence of coordinated copies lets reviewers slash it. A reputation signal can raise an identity’s limits, but cannot replace the bond. An attacker can still create many identities, yet must tie up real value in each one and risks losing it, making a Sybil swarm costly rather than free. Copper can serve as the bond’s unit, provided it has genuine market value.
